topic: database sequence mining; anomaly discovery; statistical evaluation
status: bounded research lead from one purposively selected 2010 full text; not a novelty claim
claim: The audited substring-mining paper shows fast top-k ranking by a chi-square deviation score, but its career example estimates symbol probabilities from the same 425-innings sequence and its large click-stream experiment reports only top-1 because of runtime. The evidence supports efficient optimization of the score in tested cases, not calibrated false-discovery control or reproducible anomaly discovery. A bounded follow-up is to calibrate the score on held-out sequences while accounting for the many overlapping substrings searched.
positive_evidence: For the ODI sequence, the paper bins runs into five categories, estimates their probabilities from the same career record, and identifies high- and low-scoring periods that also differ in simple observed batting summaries.

On the 989,819-record click dataset, the authors report exact top-1 results for ARLM and AGMM; the reported runtimes are 40 and 3 hours respectively versus 75+ hours for naive search and 52 hours for blocking.
Synthetic experiments report approximation ratios greater than 0.96 in tested settings, and ARLM is exact for top-1 in tested cases.
counterevidence: The exact top-1 and high synthetic approximation results are positive evidence that the proposed heuristics efficiently optimize the paper's chosen score; the finding is not that the algorithms are inaccurate.

The paper describes the score as approximating p-value significance and illustrates interpretable career periods, so the lead concerns calibration/generalization beyond the tested score and data, not the absence of useful descriptive signal.
Only a single real click dataset is used, and runtime prevented a varying top-k experiment there; this constrains both support and counterevidence.
falsifiable_test: For multiple version-pinned independent sequences, estimate expected symbol frequencies on a training window, scan all overlapping substrings in a held-out window, and compare raw chi-square rankings with multiplicity-calibrated permutation or bootstrap p-values. Preregister the event definition and report false-discovery rate, top-k stability, runtime, and confirmation on a later time window. The lead weakens if raw rankings are already well-calibrated and stable across held-out sequences, with negligible false-discovery inflation under the full scan.
limitations: One historical paper and two real datasets with different tasks; no new statistical experiment or independent replication was performed. This does not establish that the original chi-square use is invalid or estimate prevalence across database research.

topic: web data quality; probabilistic data cleaning; corruption models
status: bounded replication lead from one purposively selected 2012 full text; not a novelty claim
claim: The audited Bayesian cleaner improves repair outcomes over the tested CFD baselines in a controlled used-car experiment, but the experiment begins with one manually inspected dataset and injects known synthetic spelling, replacement, and deletion errors. This supports a concrete cross-domain validation question: do the gains persist when corruption types/rates are unknown and naturally occurring, with ground truth established independently?
positive_evidence: The paper learns generative and corruption models from dirty observations, rather than requiring a separate clean training sample in the same way as its compared CFD methods.

On roughly 10,000 used-car records, the authors report that at 1% injected noise the combined features corrected more than 31% of errors while the tested CFD methods learned no rules; across 357 injected errors, the best reported net gain was 87 clean values.
The paper measures false corrections and demonstrates a parameter tradeoff: increasing the likelihood weight reduces false positives but also reduces the number of values corrected.
counterevidence: The clean base is manually inspected and then synthetically corrupted; this provides known ground truth and controlled noise but does not reproduce uncertain, co-occurring natural web errors.
The evaluation uses one used-car schema/domain and the authors describe the results as preliminary; the observed gains cannot establish transfer to other web tables or corruption processes.
The method's correction-versus-false-positive tradeoff shows that tuning affects outcomes, so the best reported net gain is not evidence that a single setting is uniformly optimal.
falsifiable_test: Replicate on at least five independently sourced web-table domains with naturally occurring error types and a blinded adjudicated gold set; freeze the model and thresholds before each test domain. Compare against CFD, entity-resolution, and simple normalization baselines at matched labeling/tuning budgets. Report precision, recall, net corrected values, false modifications, calibration, and subgroup/domain transfer. The lead weakens if the original method's gain disappears under natural errors or is matched by simpler methods at equal annotation cost.
limitations: Single historical paper, one manually inspected source table, and synthetic corruption; no natural-noise replication or independent external benchmark was examined in this batch. The proposed test may require costly adjudicated ground truth.

topic: database privacy; graph query answering; node differential privacy
status: bounded workload-evaluation lead from one purposively selected 2013 full-version draft; not a novelty claim
claim: The recursive mechanism paper provides node- and edge-differential-privacy guarantees for a broad class of positive relational-algebra statistics, but its own experiments show that practical relative accuracy depends on privacy unit and query motif: node-private 2-star and 2-triangle counts have high relative error in the tested settings, while the edge-private triangle comparisons are favorable. A bounded follow-up is to predict and report utility by empirical sensitivity, graph density, motif, and graph size rather than summarize a mechanism with one aggregate accuracy score.
positive_evidence: The formal contribution covers approximate linear statistics over positive relational-algebra results with unrestricted joins and relates error to empirical sensitivity.

Experiments include synthetic graphs and seven real graph datasets; for reported triangle-counting comparisons, the authors say their edge-private mechanism is most accurate among the compared mechanisms.

The paper reports that the mechanism's node-private relative error for 2-star and 2-triangle counts decreases as graph size grows, providing a measurable conditional pattern rather than an unconditional failure.
counterevidence: The mechanism does establish privacy guarantees under its stated assumptions; high relative error for selected node-private graph queries is a utility limitation, not a privacy violation.

The method often outperforms comparison mechanisms in the reported settings, and empirical sensitivity is explicitly used to reason about error; topology-conditional evaluation complements rather than overturns this contribution.
The paper uses multiple real graph datasets as well as synthetic graphs, so evidence is broader than a purely toy demonstration, though still a bounded benchmark set.

sources.sections: §3-5 empirical sensitivity/error analysis; §6.1 real/synthetic subgraph-counting experiments, Figures 4-7; §8 conclusion

falsifiable_test: Re-run the mechanism and current baseline algorithms on a preregistered graph suite stratified by size, degree distribution, density, motif, and privacy unit. Match epsilon/delta, release count, implementation budget, and graph input; report absolute error, relative error, utility at fixed privacy, and runtime, with uncertainty across graph instances. Test whether empirical sensitivity and graph features predict which workloads exceed a predeclared usefulness threshold. The lead weakens if one aggregate score predicts utility across the held-out graph/motif strata and node-private 2-star/2-triangle estimates are consistently useful at matched privacy.
limitations: One historical arXiv draft; the PDF identifies a different SIGMOD 2013 version, which was not reconciled in this audit. The conclusion is specific to evaluated graph/query regimes and does not imply all node-private or relational queries are inaccurate.

topic: parallel data systems; query optimization; static program analysis
status: bounded systems-evaluation lead from one uniform-random 2012 PVLDB full text; not a novelty claim
claim: A Stratosphere prototype shows that static analysis of a small set of user-defined-function properties can unlock useful reordering in four handcrafted data flows, with measured wins up to nearly an order of magnitude between selected plans. This is evidence of feasibility, not evidence that static analysis and cost-based ranking transfer to arbitrary production UDFs: the paper itself leaves estimating black-box selectivity/cost and better search-space pruning as future work.
positive_evidence: The evaluated optimizer uses static code analysis to recover read/write properties and enumerates almost all valid alternatives identified through manual annotations on four tasks.
On four workloads, the best text-mining plan is reported to outperform the worst sampled plan by almost an order of magnitude; the best TPC-H Q15 plan is 1.4× faster than the implemented order.
Plan enumeration takes under 1,654 ms on the presented queries, showing that the prototype's overhead was small for those specific tasks.
counterevidence: All four tasks are handcrafted, and the paper identifies determining which legal reorderings are beneficial and estimating black-box selectivity/execution cost as future work.

The static analyzer is limited to compile-time-accessible information such as literal and final-variable field accesses; the authors note more exhaustive control-flow/configuration analysis is future work.
The prototype runs on a pre-release Stratosphere system; search-space growth and applicability to contemporary production runtimes are not established.

sources.sections: §5-7 property inference, plan enumeration and four-workload evaluation; §9 conclusion/future work

falsifiable_test: Port the optimizer to two independent data-flow engines and test preregistered UDF-heavy jobs from at least three application domains. Compare static-analysis-derived reorderings with manual annotations and optimizer baselines; measure semantic equivalence, enumeration overhead, top-plan runtime against exhaustive search on smaller jobs, and ranking quality under held-out input distributions. The lead weakens if static analysis misses many valid alternatives or selected plans fail to improve end-to-end runtime once input distributions shift.
limitations: One historical prototype and four handcrafted workloads; no contemporary reimplementation, independent artifact replication, or production workload study was performed.

topic: database concurrency control; serializable isolation; systems measurement
status: bounded production-systems evidence from one uniform-random 2012 PVLDB full text; not a novelty claim
claim: The PostgreSQL 9.1 SSI implementation demonstrates that serializable isolation can approach snapshot-isolation throughput in several tested workloads and outperform strict two-phase locking on read-intensive mixes, but its own measurements show overhead depends on CPU-vs-disk bottlenecks and transaction mix. The bounded follow-up is to rerun equivalent anomaly-safe workloads on current PostgreSQL builds and contemporary hardware, reporting both throughput and abort/failure behavior rather than treating one benchmark score as the cost of serializability.
positive_evidence: The paper describes an SSI implementation integrated into a production PostgreSQL release, including bounded-memory handling and interaction with replication, two-phase commit, and subtransactions.
On RUBiS, SSI reaches 422 requests/s versus 435 for snapshot isolation and 208 for S2PL; serialization failures are 0.03% for SSI versus 0.76% for S2PL in the reported setup.
In the CPU-bound in-memory DBT-2++ configuration the slowdown is 5% versus SI, while in the disk-bound configuration SSI is reported indistinguishable from SI; failure rates stay below 0.25%.
counterevidence: The SIBENCH microbenchmark reports 10–20% CPU overhead for tracking read dependencies before read-only optimizations, and read-only optimizations reduce rather than erase that cost.

The benchmark suite includes modified workloads and optimizations, and is tied to PostgreSQL 9.1-era software and 2012 hardware; it does not directly establish performance on current systems or arbitrary applications.
RUBiS shows SSI throughput below SI (422 vs 435 requests/s), so the paper does not support a literal zero-cost claim.
falsifiable_test: Run version-pinned current PostgreSQL SSI and snapshot-isolation baselines plus a correct serializable alternative across CPU-bound, disk-bound, read-heavy and mixed production-derived workloads. Hold hardware, schema, transaction mix and anomaly coverage fixed; report committed throughput, p50/p99 latency, serialization failures/retries, CPU/memory and correctness. The lead weakens if relative overhead is stable across bottleneck/mix strata and the old workload-dependent pattern does not reproduce.
limitations: One historical production implementation paper; its testbed is not current and some workloads were modified. No contemporary replication or independent trace-based benchmark was conducted.
